note: Botswana's large banks: First National Bank Botswana (the largest), Absa Bank Botswana and Stanbic Bank Botswana. FNB Botswana's retail tariff guide (effective 1 February 2025, still the latest on its site: a 2026 guide answered 404) and its lending rates for October 2026 were read: its four credit cards, the Firstcard, Gold, Platinum and Private Clients cards (sold by the holder's income band, which the game doesn't check), cost P157.50, P221.60, P253.10 and P273.40 a year, a joining fee of P109.35 and P8.05 for a cash withdrawal at FNB's own ATMs (P11.50 at another local ATM, P52.80 abroad; the own-ATM fee is written); credit cards bear a nominal 22% to 28% a year, written at the top with its lowest as from. The guide states no late, over-limit or foreign transaction fee for the cards. Absa Botswana's site lists no tariff guide (its rates and fees page answered 404), and Stanbic Botswana's wasn't found; neither is written. Wave 4 (30 October 2026), for a second and third bank: Absa Bank Botswana's tariff guide (effective 22 April 2025, the one its site links) gives its Absa credit cards' joining fees (P216.79 Classic and Gold, P360.85 Signature), fees to hold (P216.79 a year Classic and Gold, P2,395.37 a year Platinum, P128.88 a month Signature), cash advance (2.28%, at least P34.78, at most P349.97), late (P32.96), over-limit (P65.91) and unpaid (P131.81) fees, and its lending rates for October 2026 give credit cards a nominal 24% to 36% (34.49% average effective) without saying the period it is charged by, so, as the rule for a rate without its period requires, Absa's cards aren't written. Stanbic Bank Botswana's tariff guide (effective 1 July 2026) gives its personal Silver, Gold and Platinum credit cards' annual fees (P141.36, P212.04, P471.18) but an interest rate (28.00% a year) only for its corporate card, so its personal cards aren't written. So FNB stays the only bank written. Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: No minimum payment is published for FNB Botswana's four cards; tried: its credit card, Classic, Gold and Platinum pages and its card calculator (read 2026-10-30, none states a share), its 2025 tariff guide (none), a search in English (only Absa Botswana's '5% to 100%', another bank), and archive.org's API (no answer); the Bank of Botswana's rules weren't searched for want of the budget.
